body.justification: This theorem makes fixed support a semantics-preserving reduction rather than a graph simplification that silently enlarges the model.
body.gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser define selector gates, while Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give finite response types; neither supplies inverse parameter maps for support-active gate substitution.
body.consumer: Every subsequent formula and twin certificate can be checked against the original selector-gated SCM rather than an enlarged latent projection.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(E=E_H\).  Finiteness of every alphabet, from \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\), makes every structural response table and every latent-root mass vector a finite list.  Thus the coordinate operations below are literal operations on finite products of simplices.

First take \(\theta\in\Theta_H\).  By the definition of \(\nu_H\), every primitive natural-response probability and every latent-root probability is copied to its tagged coordinate of \(\Lambda_H\).  The copied coordinates are nonnegative and each primitive table sums to one.  Two normalized occurrences produced from one primitive table receive the same coordinate, so every coordinate-copy equation in \(g_H=0\) holds.  The deterministic multiplexer equations hold because the selector gates are known by \(\textnormal{ass:known-selector-gates}\), and the root-factorization equations hold by \(\textnormal{ass:latent-root-independence}\).  Recursive evaluation of the stored selector equation gives
\[
s_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}(s)=p_\theta(S=s).
\]
Consequently \(s_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}(s)>0\) if and only if \(s\in H\), by \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\).  The same recursive evaluation on a supported context gives
\[
o_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}(c)=p_\theta(c)>0,
\qquad c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+),
\]
where the last inequality is part of \(\textnormal{def:model-class}\).  Hence every defining condition of \(\mathcal I_H\) holds and
\[
\nu_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathcal I_H. \tag{1}
\]

Conversely, let \(\eta\in\mathcal I_H\).  Read one probability vector from each equivalence class of tagged occurrences and retain each dormant vector.  This is well defined because the coordinate-copy equations in \(g_H(\eta)=0\) make all occurrences in an equivalence class equal.  Each read vector lies in its prescribed simplex because \(\eta\in\Lambda_H\).  Reinsert the stored zero-one selector multiplexers and retain the declared recursive order.  The root-factorization equations in \(g_H(\eta)=0\) supply exactly the independent-root factorization required by \(G^+\).  This constructs \(\rho_H(\eta)\in\Theta(G^+)\).  By construction of the polynomial evaluators,
\[
p_{\rho_H(\eta)}(S=s)=s_H^N(\eta)(s),
\qquad
p_{\rho_H(\eta)}(c)=o_H^N(\eta)(c).
\]
The support and strict-positivity clauses in the definition of \(\mathcal I_H\) therefore give exact selector support \(H\) and positivity on every admissible cell.  All remaining membership conditions in \(\textnormal{def:model-class}\) hold from the retained table simplices, reinserted gates, recursive order, and root equations.  Hence \(\rho_H(\eta)\in\Theta_H\).  Reinsertion reads every active and dormant primitive coordinate exactly once, while normalization copies it back to all and only the occurrences prescribed by \(g_H\).  Therefore
\[
\nu_H\{\rho_H(\eta)\}=\eta. \tag{2}
\]
Likewise, no primitive coordinate of \(\theta\) is deleted, including a dormant coordinate, and so
\[
\rho_H\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=\theta. \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) prove that the maps are mutual inverses.  In particular, (2) also gives the reverse inclusion to (1), and hence \(\mathcal I_H=\nu_H(\Theta_H)\).

It remains to compare executions rather than merely coordinates.  Couple \(\theta\) and \(\nu_H(\theta)\) by using the same realization of every retained response type and latent root.  Fix \(e\in E\).  Induct along the recursive order from \(\textnormal{ass:recursive-equations}\).  At an uncontrolled node the two response tables and already evaluated parents agree.  At a selector-controlled node, either the gate remains explicit and agrees, or the relevant selector component was substituted because it is constant on all of \(E\), so its value at \(e\) equals the substituted value.  Thus the node values agree at every induction step.  For \(e=s\in H\), summing the common pointwise indicators over the same latent-root law proves
\[
O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=O_H(\theta).
\]
For \(e=s_\emptyset\), after additionally setting \(A=a\), the same induction proves
\[
T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\]
Using the bijection between \(\Theta_H\) and \(\mathcal I_H\) in these two equalities proves equality of the two attainable observed-target relations.  Notice that the argument used only executions in \(E_H\); it introduced no unsupported selector value.
